scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants that circumstances create leaders, then argues personal qualities matter just as much; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose at about 400 words on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: We often wonder whether great leaders are born or simply shaped by their times.
Some people argue that leaders are created by the demands that are placed on them.
I agree that difficult circumstances often bring out leaders, but I believe a person's own qualities and choices matter just as much.
First, it is true that hard situations often turn ordinary people into leaders.
When a crisis demands action, someone usually rises to meet the challenge and guide others.
For example, many wartime leaders were quiet, unremarkable figures until danger forced them to step forward.
This shows that pressure and need can draw out abilities people never knew they had.
A serious challenge can give a person both the chance and the reason to lead.
Without such demands, many capable leaders might have lived ordinary and forgotten lives.
To this extent, circumstances clearly play a large part in creating leaders.
Second, however, demands alone cannot create a leader from someone who lacks the right qualities.
Faced with the same crisis, many people panic or freeze while only a few are able to lead.
Consider two officials in the same emergency, where one collapses under pressure and the other inspires calm.
Such differences show that courage, character, and judgment come from within the person.
Leaders also shape their circumstances through their own choices rather than only responding to them.
The very same demands can produce a hero in one person and a failure in another.
Personal qualities, then, are as important as the situations that call them forth.
In conclusion, the demands of a situation can certainly help create leaders.
But those demands only reveal leadership in people who already possess the necessary strengths.
True leaders emerge where difficult circumstances meet the character ready to rise to them.
